full_voiceover_script: Long before the Renaissance in Europe, an intellectual explosion in ninth-century Baghdad laid the foundation for modern mathematics, optics, and astronomy. At the center of it all stood Bayt al-Hikma—the House of Wisdom. Here, polymath Al-Khwarizmi developed the principles of algebra and algorithmic computation. In physics and optics, Ibn al-Haytham overturned ancient beliefs, proving that light travels in straight lines and pioneering the modern empirical scientific method. Observatories mapped celestial coordinates with astonishing precision, constructing brass astrolabes that guided explorers across uncharted deserts and oceans. This is the golden legacy that reshaped human civilization.
